name: combined_gas_steam_cycle
title: Combined gas-steam cycle (Brayton topping cycle, Rankine bottoming cycle)
summary: Combined gas-steam cycle: a gas turbine (Brayton) topping cycle on ideal-gas air whose exhaust gases heat a simple Rankine cycle on water in a heat exchanger; computes the steam-to-gas flow ratio of the heat exchanger and the thermal efficiency of the combined cycle.
language_features: arrays (state points P[i], T[i], h[i], s[i], x[i] and P_TGV[i], T_TGV[i], h_TGV[i], s_TGV[i])
property functions (ideal-gas air and real water)

authors: TBD (ULiège Thermodynamics Laboratory, course Thermodynamique appliquée)

verification.reference: EES stored solution of the source file R07_E05_2022.EES (44 variables), compared with tools/compare_solution.py --ees-units
verification.notes: 27 of the 36 common variables agree within 7.4e-06 relative (worst case h[1]); the 9 excluded variables are the absolute h and s of air, which carry the reference-state offset between the EES Air_ha and CoolProp Air models (+126.06 kJ/kg on h, -2.978 kJ/kg-K on s at 300 K and 1 bar): through their differences the air agrees to 4.9e-06. compare_solution.py prints '36 common variables, 9 differ (rtol=0.001)'. Only in EES: m_dot_TGV, m_dot_ORC, W_dot_turb_TGV, W_dot_cp_TGV, W_dot_turb_ORC, W_dot_pump_ORC, effet_utile, effet_couteux, entries of the EES variable list that appear only in the commented-out equations of the original and were removed as dead code. Only in CoolSolve: T_TGV[2], s_TGV[2], s_TGV[4], s_TGV[5], T[1], T[2], T[4], x[4], the post-processing state points added for the diagrams. The gas cycle is on the ideal-gas substance Air in place of the EES humid-air pseudo-fluid 'Air_ha', which CoolSolve cannot evaluate above 623.15 K (CS-BUG-HUMIDAIR-HIGHT).
